guidelines.detail: same as LRN-006 (The description says the solution is implemented 'whether it's a fix, training, or policy change'. The generated model keeps one task labeled with all three alternatives and has no exclusive split or merge around them. The reference has separate tasks for the training and policy-change alternatives (M1, M3) and an exclusive gateway split and merge around the alternatives (M4). This is the same sit)

same as LRN-022 (The generator merged the three named ways of implementing the solution (fix, training, policy change) into one task labelled 'Implement solution'. The reference keeps 'Implement fix', 'Conduct training' and 'Change policy' as separate tasks, so the 'Change policy' and 'Conduct training' tasks are missing and the remaining one is matched only by label similarity (P3). The description states the alt)

same as LRN-013 (The reference has a reporting task ('Report incident') after a plain start event, and the generated model has neither that task nor a matching start event, although the description opens with an actor reporting an incident and then gives the following steps. LRN-013 already covers this pattern, so the guideline is a restatement of it in generic terms. The parallel-gateway differences (M2, M3) are )

same as LRN-010 (The reference splits the team's listed activities (gather information, identify cause, propose corrective actions) into parallel branches with a split after the assignment step and a join before the proposal step. The generated model instead chained the assignment directly into the first listed activity and sequenced the activities (M2, M3, G2, F1). This is the exact pattern LRN-010 addresses, so )

same as LRN-004 (M4 shows the reference start event has no counterpart, and M1 shows the reference task for the reported action is missing. Together they indicate the generator folded the reporting action into the start event. S1 states that the process begins when an employee or customer reports an incident, followed by internal steps (S2, S3). LRN-004 already requires a plain start event followed by a task for t)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states one step that can be carried out in one of several named ways, joined by 'or' within the same clause, and the step is followed by a later step that depends on which way was chosen: Model each named way of carrying out the step as its own task. Place an exclusive gateway split before these tasks, with a labeled outgoing flow to each task. Join the alternative tasks with an exclusive gateway merge before the next step. Do not collapse the alternatives into one generic task, and do not keep only one of the named alternatives.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states one step that can be carried out in one of several named alternative ways, introduced by 'whether it is ... or ...' or an equivalent enumeration, and the following steps are described in a way that is not the same for every alternative

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states one sentence or step in which several distinct actions are chained on the same objects, or in which one outcome is delivered through alternative means (for example 'via X or Y'): Model each distinct action and each alternative means as its own task, in the order the description gives. If the description says one alternative is chosen, place the alternative tasks behind a decision gateway; if it does not choose, keep them as separate tasks on their own flow. Do not combine them into one task whose label lists them together.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states one step as a choice among several named alternatives joined by 'whether it is X, Y, or Z' (or similar), and the description does not say that the step must also be carried out in every alternative form

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description joins two activities with 'and' (for example, one party performs both actions for the same case) and gives no stated order between them, so both must be completed before the flow continues: Model the two activities as parallel branches: place a parallel gateway split before them and a parallel gateway join after them, so the next step starts only when both branches have completed. Do not model them as a sequence with an arbitrary order, and do not model them as alternatives.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names several activities that one team performs for the same case, joined by commas and 'and' in one sentence without explicit sequencing words, and a later activity starts only after all of them are done

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process begins when a participant performs an identifying or recognizing action, and then gives the steps of the work that follows: Model a plain start event that carries no action label, followed by a task named after the participant's performed action. Connect the subsequent steps after that task, in the order the description gives. Do not make the performed action a start event or label the start event with the state it produces.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process begins when an actor performs a reporting or identifying action, and then gives the steps of the work that follows

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists three or more activities with no stated order between them, joined by commas and 'and', and all of them must be completed before a later step begins: Model each listed activity as its own task on a separate outgoing branch of one parallel gateway split, and rejoin all branches with a parallel gateway join before the next step. Do not sequence the activities in the order they are listed, and do not use an exclusive gateway for them.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists three or more activities performed by the same party in one sentence, joined by commas and 'and', with no stated order between them, and a later step begins only after all of them are completed

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a process or phase begins when a participant performs an action (for example, a participant identifies a need), or that a later phase begins after a state change, and then gives the steps of the work that follows: Model the participant's performed action as a task in the flow, placed after a start event that carries no action label. Do not turn the action into a start event, an end event, or a subprocess named after its resulting state. Use a subprocess only when the description gives a multi-step phase with its own internal steps, and keep the action that initiates that phase as a separate task before it. Model the phase's final state as the end of the flow only when the description states it as the process outcome.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process begins when a participant (internal or external, such as an employee or customer) performs a reporting action, and then gives the internal steps that follow the report
